## Finding

Yes. The September work order has a cost event created after the cost period entered Pending Close.

| Field | Finding |
|---|---|
| Work order | **WO-2025-09-004** — **MO-25-09-1070** |
| Source transaction | **TXN-ISSUE-250930-1070** |
| Event | **CE-250904-0004** — INPUT |
| Amount | **28,476,342 cents** (**$284,763.42**) |
| Event-created time | **2025-09-30T19:15:00** |
| September Pending Close time | **2025-09-30T18:00:00** |
| Time late | **75 minutes** |
| Recorded accounting status | **POSTED** |

The recorded **POSTED** status is **not consistent** with the supplied Oracle Fusion Cloud SCM Cost Management 26B policy. It says newly created transactions falling in or before a Pending Close period are not staged for Cost Accounting or Receipt Accounting until the period is closed or reopened. This event is an INPUT transaction, not one of the listed policy exceptions.

Times are reported as recorded; the source does not specify a time zone. The review was read-only.

I used the current assessment **RSK-EPGGL-2025Q3-CUR** for *Epic Games, Inc. v. Google LLC et al.*—not an older assessment under a historical case-name variant.

Applying **both** conditions together—partly supported evidence and active remediation—the complete qualifying set is:

| Control ID | Restriction code | Testing state | Evidence reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| CTL-EPGGL-PI-004 | THIRD-PARTY-CATALOG-ACCESS | Retest scheduled | EVD-EPGGL-PI-2025-0062 |
| CTL-EPGGL-PI-010 | REVIEW-PROCESS-SLA | Design review | EVD-EPGGL-PI-2025-0079 |

Both controls share an implementation deadline of **June 7, 2025**. As of **September 30, 2025**, that deadline was **115 calendar days past**.
